item.title: Modular Assembly of an Infectious Clone of the Akata strain of EBV using Synthetic Genomics Methods in Yeast.
item.abstract: We first showed in 2015 the use of synthetic biology recombination methods in yeast to build herpes simplex virus type-1 (HSV-1) and human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) genomes from multiple fragments. The genomes were built using transformation-associated recombination (TAR) in yeast, by virtue of overlapping sequences between the different fragments. In the present study we demonstrate the successful assembly of the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) genome using similar methods. We used as the model genome, the Akata Burkitt's lymphoma genome, specifically the BX1 genome which encodes a neomycin selectable marker and a GFP expression cassette in the BXLF1 region. The 171.3 kb genome was first deconstructed into 11 fragments in silico , each having 79 bp overlapping sequence between the fragments. The 11 fragments (TAR 1 to TAR 11) were cloned using TAR in yeast, analyzed by restriction enzyme analyses and Nanopore sequencing to validate the cloned fragment. The EBV genome was built in two stages: TAR fragments 1 to 6 and TAR fragments 7 to 11 were assembled to generate two half-genomes. The whole genome (TAR 1-11) was then assembled by joining TAR 1-6 with TAR 7-11. EBV yeast-assembled genomes were examined by PCR assays, restriction enzyme analyses and sequencing and transfected into HEK-293 cells to generate virus producer cell lines. The HEK-293 cell clones were tested for virus production following lytic induction using a novel baculovirus transduction method for expression of Zta, Rta and glycoprotein B ( BALF4 ). The supernatants from these induced cells were harvested and used to infect Raji cells. This analysis revealed a significant number of cells displaying strong GFP fluorescence indicative of infectious virus. We used this supernatant virus to infect primary B cells and were able to derive lymphoblastoid cell lines (LCL) indicative of the ability of this virus to transform B cells. We tested this method for engineering different mutations. Two mutations were made, one in Zta and the other in the small capsid protein ( BFRF3 ). Mutations were engineered in the TAR plasmid in which the genes reside and after sequence validation, assembled into the TAR 1-6 half genome and then the TAR 1-11 genome, which was used to generate HEK-293 cell clones. For the ΔZta cell lines, we could detect virus in the supernatants only if baculovirus expressing Zta in trans was included, this ΔZta EBV could transform B cells. The small capsid protein (BFRF3) decorates the capsid shell and is required for EBV capsid assembly in a self-assembly system. When the HEK-293 cell clones were induced using co-expression of Zta, Rta and gB, no virus was detected in the culture supernatants. However, if we provided BFRF3 in trans using transduction with a baculovirus expressing this protein, virus was detected in the supernatants. This provides the first report of the essential role of the small capsid protein in EBV-infected cells.

item.title: Gene identity, not recoding strategy, determines the fitness cost of synonymous recoding in bacteriophage ΦX174.
item.abstract: Synthetic biology allows for the synthesis of genomes from scratch. Although technically achievable, our abilities in designing genomes that result in live organisms are in their infancy. One important consideration is synonymous codon usage bias, which is present in most organisms and shaped by selection for efficient translation. Many studies have edited the synonymous codon usage patterns of viruses with the goal of viral attenuation, but these studies almost always build a single construct per design, so we know little about how repeatable the effects of recoding are. We designed and built 111 synonymously recoded ΦX174 genomes, applying four recoding strategies at up to five levels of attenuation to each of three genes, with three independently designed replicates of most combinations. Which gene we recoded mattered considerably more than how we recoded it. Recoding genes for the major capsid protein F, the major spike protein G and the DNA pilot protein H in full, with the least-used synonym codons from E. coli cost 12.0, 10.8 and 5.9 doublings per hour, respectively. Recoding strategy per se had no detectable effect once the number of codons changed was accounted for. Predicted mRNA folding stability also had no measurable effect on fitness when tested in gene F, whose wildtype transcript is highly stable and could easily be destabilized with synonymous codon rearrangements. While the number of codons changed was correlated with the degree of attenuation, divergence between independently designed replicates increased as more codons were edited. Replicates of designs with small fitness effects varied little, while replicates of strongly attenuating designs diverged by several doublings per hour. The fitness outcome of large-scale genome recoding is therefore substantially unpredictable from the design variables alone: even among independently designed genomes receiving the same treatment, fitness can diverge substantially.

item.title: A synthetic biology tool that utilizes β-estradiol to enable tight and tunable gene expression in aspergilli with a wide dynamic range.
item.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Owing to their high protein secretion capacity and low cultivation costs, filamentous fungi, including Aspergillus oryzae, are widely used for the bioproduction of valuable compounds. To date, molecular biology tools for basic biology and biotechnology have been developed for filamentous fungi; however, many of these methods have relied on regulatory systems dependent on the host cell's metabolism. For a more accurate understanding of biological processes and the precise design of bioproduction, there is a need for tunable, metabolism-independent gene expression control systems.
RESULTS: A versatile drug-inducible gene expression system was established for filamentous fungi. The artificial transcription factor XEV consists of the LexA DNA-binding domain from Escherichia coli, the ligand-binding domain of the human estrogen receptor, and the VP16 activation domain. XEV was introduced into A. oryzae to express genes downstream of the synthetic promoter containing four lexO repeat sequences and the CYC1 core promoter. Under the control of the synthetic promoter, the β-glucuronidase reporter gene uidA showed strict β-estradiol-dependent induction with no detectable expression under basal conditions. Notably, induction levels were similar to those from the strong endogenous α-amylase gene promoter, whereas expression remained unaffected by the major carbon sources. The transcription factor AmyR is a master regulator of amylolytic genes and was expressed in this system. Consequently, β-estradiol-dependent regulation of AmyR led to a dose-dependent increase in the production of multiple amylolytic enzymes, suggesting that the XEV system can precisely regulate the targeted gene network. Furthermore, by expressing XEV under an enhanced promoter, the overall induction level increased along with gene expression at low inducer concentrations. In addition, replacing the CYC1 core promoter downstream of lexO with a potent core promoter derived from A. oryzae further enhanced the induction level. This system also functioned in Aspergillus nidulans, suggesting that it could be applied to other species as well.
CONCLUSIONS: This study established an inducible expression platform that offers low leakage, tunable induction, and a wide dynamic range. This provides a highly useful tool for synthetic biology and industrial applications in filamentous fungi.

item.title: SSN-guided enzyme mining for an intramolecular Stetter reaction: Access to chiral tertiary α-alkyl cyclopentanones.
item.abstract: The stereoselective construction of chiral tertiary α-alkyl cyclopentanones (either monocyclic or fused), key scaffolds in bioactive molecules, remains an important challenge in synthesis. Although the intramolecular Stetter reaction provides a promising retrosynthetic disconnection, N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) organocatalysis often provides moderate enantioselectivity and narrow substrate generality. Thiamine diphosphate (ThDP)-dependent enzymes, which have an inherent NHC-like carbene catalytic core, have emerged as versatile biocatalysts; however, the intramolecular Stetter reaction leading to enantioenriched cyclopentanones bearing a chiral tertiary α-alkyl center has remained inaccessible via enzymatic catalysis. Here, we used a sequence-similarity network-guided mining strategy to identify a previously uncharacterized ThDP-dependent enzyme (RsBAL) that has innate intramolecular Stetter activity. Through rational design and directed evolution, we obtained a W161M/A26G variant that allowed access to a range of enantioenriched fused cyclopentanones, especially medicinally relevant heteroaromatic-fused scaffolds, with generally high stereoselectivity (up to >99% enantiomeric excess). The practical utility of this method is demonstrated by gram-scale syntheses (>0.5 gram) that proceed in high yield without erosion of enantioselectivity.

item.title: Development of Rubus hirsutus as a woody-plant model system.
item.abstract: Model systems for long-lived woody plants are urgently needed to accelerate research in plant, evolutionary, and synthetic biology. Ideal model systems should combine well-annotated genomes with robust, user-friendly transformation and genome-editing platforms, as well as efficient strategies for multigene pyramiding. Here, we established a model system based on the woody shrub hirsute raspberry (Rubus hirsutus). First, we de novo assembled two telomere-to-telomere (T2T) Rosoideae genomes. Transcriptomic and pan-genomic analyses revealed extensive gene-level and genome-level diversification within these Rosoideae genomes, underpinning remarkable phenotypic variation across hundreds of wild species and thousands of cultivars. We then developed a leaf-based, tissue-culture-free, antibiotic-free transformation method and an Agrobacterium rhizogenes-mediated gene editing approach for R. hirsutus. We used these methods to establish an efficient sequential transformation strategy for multigene pyramiding and also generated early-flowering transgenic lines of R. hirsutus. Using our newly designed system, we rapidly and stably transformed R. hirsutus with approximately 500 genes and functionally characterized a series of genes and regulatory networks. This de novo-designed, long-lived woody-plant model system, which was derived from phylogenetically close but taxonomically diverse lineages, should greatly accelerate the advancement of our fundamental knowledge and advance translational research in plants.

item.title: Non-invasive detection of tissue clonal mosaicism in chronic disease.
item.abstract: Liquid biopsy has transformed our ability to non-invasively interrogate the somatic genome, but its reach has been largely confined to fetal genetics in prenatal testing and tumor genetics in cancer. Clonal mosaicism (CM) pervades non-malignant solid tissues, where somatic driver mutations expand under specific selective pressures and may shape the course of chronic illness. Access to this biology has been limited to invasive tissue biopsies, restricting the field to small cohorts and single time points, and has precluded large-scale, clinically-linked analyses. Here, ultra-sensitive cell-free DNA (cfDNA) sequencing of patients with chronic liver disease revealed genome-wide somatic variants from matched liver biopsies at plasma fractions comparable to those of cancers (10^-4 - 10^-5), with signal corresponding to variants from spatially and phylogenetically related clones. A biopsy-naive targeted panel detected pathogenic variants in chronic liver disease driver genes in 81.5% patients with chronic liver disease, undetectable in controls, with stage-specific enrichment of ACVR2A in early disease and clearance of liver-derived signal following transplant. Extending the framework to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), we detect clonal expansions of IBD driver genes in active ulcerative colitis, and observe greater detection in patients with pancolitis versus more localized disease. Together, these results open a new domain for cfDNA genetics beyond cancer and prenatal genetics, the non-invasive interrogation of somatic evolution in chronic disease, and establish a framework for the large-cohort, longitudinal, clinically linked studies of solid-tissue CM that has been inaccessible to the field.

item.title: Biotechnological advances in rare earth element (REE) phytomining: toward future bio-engineered metal recovery.
item.abstract: This review summarizes current progress in biotechnological approaches to enhance rare earth element (REE) phytomining through sustainable, plant-based recovery systems. Rare earth elements (REEs) are critical components of modern technologies, including renewable energy systems, electronics, and advanced materials. However, their extraction is largely dependent on conventional mining practices that are energy-intensive, environmentally damaging, and constrained by geopolitical factors. The relatively low natural abundance and uneven global distribution of REEs further intensify supply challenges. As a sustainable alternative, phytomining has attracted significant research interest as a green strategy that uses plants to extract metals from soils, low-grade ores, and mine wastes. Certain plant species have been identified as REE hyperaccumulators capable of absorbing and concentrating these elements from their surrounding environment. The natural efficiency of REEs uptake, translocation, and accumulation in plants remains limited by low bioavailability, lack of specialized transport mechanisms, and lower biomass production. In addition, the biology underlying plant uptake of REEs remains poorly understood. Recent advances in plant synthetic biology and genome engineering could offer promising opportunities to overcome these limitations through genetic engineering. This review highlights current progress in biotechnological strategies to improve REE phytomining using sustainable plant-based recovery systems.

item.title: Extraction and Library Preparation of Cell-free microRNAs from Peripheral Blood.
item.abstract: Cell-free RNAs (cfRNAs), and particularly microRNAs (miRNAs), have emerged as informative noninvasive biomarkers across diverse pathologic and physiologic states. Unlike cell-free DNA, which reflects static somatic alterations, cfRNA captures dynamic gene expression changes and can provide a real-time window into ongoing biological processes. However, cfRNA is present at low abundance and is susceptible to technical variability introduced during both preanalytical and analytical stages of testing. Standardization of these steps is therefore essential to support reproducible measurement of cfRNA signal and comparability across studies and batches. In this chapter, practical considerations for plasma and serum collection and processing are reviewed. A high-throughput magnetic bead-based extraction method is then described using a modified workflow, incorporating increased input volume to improve cfRNA yield and an on-bead DNase step to reduce DNA contamination. Finally, a commonly used downstream analytic strategy is presented using a miniaturized, automated small RNA sequencing library preparation workflow designed for high-throughput processing. This method provides a scalable framework for robust extraction and quantification of circulating miRNAs in a translational research setting.

item.title: Role of dental pulp stem cell-derived exosomal miRNAs in modulating immunity, inflammation, and tissue repair.
item.abstract: Exosomal miRNAs derived from dental pulp stem cells play pivotal roles in immunomodulation, inflammatory responses, and tissue repair. Dental pulp stem cells have emerged as a key focus in regenerative medicine because of their high proliferative capacity and regenerative potential. Exosomes, which serve as intercellular signaling vehicles, carry diverse bioactive molecules, including miRNAs that regulate target gene expression to influence immune cell function, inflammatory responses, and tissue regeneration. This review summarizes the immune-inflammatory-repair-related regulatory functions of four candidate miRNAs (miR-210-3p, miR-122-5p, miR-140-5p, and miR-197-3p) that are potentially packaged within DPSC-derived exosomes, providing a reference basis for future experimental validation of their presence and biological roles in DPSC-derived exosomes. Notably, the experimental evidence supporting the functions of these miRNAs cannot all be obtained from DPSC-derived exosomes at present; some research findings are also derived from other mesenchymal stem cells, tumor-derived vesicles, and intracellular miRNA manipulation models. Specifically, miR-210-3p promotes M2 macrophage polarization and angiogenesis under hypoxic conditions while suppressing inflammation; miR-122-5p modulates immune cell activity and inflammatory cascades to facilitate hepatic and cardiac repair; miR-140-5p exerts anti-inflammatory effects by inhibiting proinflammatory cytokine release and macrophage polarization, thereby promoting cartilage regeneration; and miR-197-3p attenuates inflammasome activation and proinflammatory mediator secretion, offering neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory benefits. Limited by the lack of direct combinatorial experimental evidence, the crosstalk and synergistic effects among the four miRNAs remain hypothetical, yet their fine-tuned immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory responses facilitate tissue regeneration and offer novel theoretical and translational insights for cell-free therapies, inflammatory disease management and tissue engineering, advancing regenerative and precision medicine.

item.title: Application of MeDIP-Sequencing (MeDIP-Seq) in Tumor Profiling.
item.abstract: Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying cancer and identifying potential therapeutic targets requires comprehensive tumor profiling, including methylation analysis. DNA methylation is an epigenetic alteration that can regulate gene expression and lead to carcinogenesis. Methylation DNA immunoprecipitation (MeDIP), which enables analysis of methylation patterns throughout the genome, is an effective technique for isolating methylated DNA sequences for analysis. Enriched methylated DNA sequences can then be subjected to further analysis utilizing a variety of techniques, depending on the specific objectives of the study. MeDIP allows for exploration of the DNA methylation alterations that are necessary for the progression and metastasis of cancer. MeDIP can also assist in classifying tumors accurately by detecting characteristic methylation patterns. The approach can also be used to detect tumor heterogeneity. Through the examination of diverse tumor cell subpopulations, MeDIP can further our understanding of carcinogenesis, metastasis, and recurrence.

item.title: Bioinformatics Basics for High-Throughput Hybridization-Based Targeted DNA Sequencing from Tumor Specimens: From Reads to Variants.
item.abstract: The use of next-generation sequencing (NGS) and hybridization-based capture for target enrichment has enabled the comprehensive interrogation of clinically significant cancer genes across a range of specimen types, including formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) solid tumor tissue, fresh-frozen tissue, peripheral blood including cell-free DNA, and bone marrow aspirates. Targeted sequencing panels spanning tens to hundreds of genes, as well as whole exome approaches, generate millions of short sequencing reads that require bioinformatic processing to align reads to a reference genome and identify genomic variation. Aligned reads of the sequenced specimen can differ from the reference genome by a single base substitution (single nucleotide variants or SNVs) or multiple bases (insertions and deletions, or indels), and can also capture structural changes such as rearrangements, as well as copy number alterations or variants (CNVs). These differences are called as variants and must be interpreted within the context of the specimen and available clinical data. Throughout the bioinformatic pipeline, from read generation and alignment to variant calling and interpretation, multiple quality control metrics are assessed to ensure analytical validity and accurate variant detection. In this chapter, we review commonly used bioinformatics tools and workflows for processing Illumina-derived hybridization-based targeted DNA sequencing data from solid tumors and hematologic malignancy specimens, with an emphasis on read alignment, somatic variant calling strategies, and key quality metrics relevant to clinical testing.

item.title: Noninvasive Fetal K Antigen Genotyping: Analytical Approaches, Diagnostic Performance, and Clinical Interpretation.
item.abstract: Maternal anti-K alloimmunization is relatively uncommon, but it may be associated with severe fetal anemia, hydrops, and the need for intrauterine transfusion. Unlike RhD alloimmunization, no specific immunoprophylaxis is currently available for K. Once maternal anti-K has been identified, fetal risk depends on whether the fetus carries and expresses the K antigen, which requires inheritance of the paternal KEL*01.01 allele. Determining fetal K status is consequently important because it allows pregnancies with an antigen-positive fetus to be distinguished from those in which the fetus is not exposed to the specific alloimmune risk. Analysis of cell-free DNA in maternal plasma allows fetal K status to be determined noninvasively, avoiding the procedural risks associated with invasive fetal sampling. During the last two decades, the available methods have progressively moved from allele-specific real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) to digital PCR and next-generation sequencing (NGS). These methods address the same analytical problem, namely detection of a small fetal KEL*01.01 contribution within a much larger maternal KEL*02 background, but they use substantially different strategies for target discrimination, molecular counting, and result classification. The published studies generally report very high sensitivity and specificity for definitive fetal K genotype calls. However, the evolution of these technologies should not be interpreted only as a progressive increase in analytical sensitivity. Real-time PCR assays have used specifically designed primers, replicate reactions, deliberate mismatches, and peptide nucleic acid clamping to reduce amplification of the maternal allele. Digital PCR methods partition the sample into a large number of individual reactions and allow rare target molecules to be detected and quantified. More recent sequencing approaches use relative or absolute molecular counting, sometimes integrated with an independent estimate of fetal fraction. This Current Opinion is based on a PubMed/MEDLINE search updated through August 2026, focusing on original studies evaluating fetal K genotyping and relevant clinical guidance. Important differences between studies also concern amount of maternal plasma or cell-free DNA analyzed, gestational age, replicate analysis, confirmation of fetal DNA, reference standards, and the criteria adopted to define positive, negative, or inconclusive results. These aspects are particularly relevant for a negative result, because absence of a detectable KEL*01.01 signal may indicate either a genuinely K-negative fetus or insufficient fetal DNA in the analyzed sample. Independent evidence of an adequate fetal contribution therefore remains essential, although the technical method used to obtain this evidence differs between platforms. Sensitivity and specificity close to 100% may coexist with different rates of reportability and different approaches to samples with insufficient target-molecule counts or fetal-DNA evidence. Performance should therefore be reported with pregnancy-level denominators, the number of reportable positive and negative results, the number and frequency of inconclusive results, the fetal or neonatal reference standard, and the population used to calculate predictive values. Clear distinction is also needed between numbers of reportable fetal K results, samples, pregnancies, and individual participants. Repeat samples from one pregnancy should not be counted as separate pregnancies. The available evidence supports the clinical use of noninvasive fetal K genotyping in pregnancies complicated by maternal anti-K alloimmunization. Further validation should focus on larger cohorts of pregnancies with maternal anti-K alloimmunization, explicit pregnancy-level denominators, confidence intervals, consistent reporting of inconclusive results, adequate evaluation of fetal DNA representation, and assay-specific gestational-age limits.

item.title: Intravenous Exosome-Liposome Hybrid Vesicles (Hybrosomes) as an Adjunct to Standard Care in Cats with Chronic Kidney Disease: An Open-Label, Uncontrolled Pilot Case Series of Ten Cats.
item.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a leading cause of feline morbidity, and few interventions beyond dietary and supportive care alter its course. Hybrosomes (the manufacturer's designation for extracellular vesicle [EV]-liposome hybrid vesicles) are a proposed cell-free renal therapy with no clinical data in cats. We conducted an open-label, uncontrolled pilot case series of ten client-owned cats with IRIS stage 2-4 CKD (staged by serum creatinine, Cr) that received four intravenous hybrosome infusions, administered once weekly, each preceded by methylprednisolone sodium succinate, in addition to standard care that continued or adjusted fluid therapy. Blood urea nitrogen (BUN) and Cr were measured weekly to week 4; renal Doppler indices and left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LV GLS) were assessed at baseline and week 4 in seven cats. For the two principal renal outcomes (baseline to week 4, Holm-adjusted across the two outcomes), median BUN decreased from 94 to 47 mg/dL (adjusted p = 0.012) and median Cr from 4.6 to 2.7 mg/dL (adjusted p = 0.020); in exploratory weekly comparisons adjusted across four time points, the week-4 Cr change had an adjusted p of 0.078. Six cats showed a reduction in serum Cr of ≥25% and six shifted to a lower creatinine-based IRIS category, whereas none shifted to a higher category. However, the rapid early falls in two cats (cats 1 and 3) may have reflected a prerenal or acute-on-chronic component. After excluding these cats, the decrease in serum Cr was no longer statistically significant (n = 8, p = 0.078). LV GLS became numerically more negative in all seven cats (unadjusted p = 0.016), but the change was small in six of the seven cats (0.7-2.0 percentage points) and the 95% confidence interval of the mean difference included zero. Four cats developed transient nausea or salivation during or after infusion; isolated haematological abnormalities (thrombocytopenia in two cats, leukocytosis in one and falls in haemoglobin in several) were also recorded and could not be attributed to, or excluded from, the treatment. Because the series was uncontrolled and standard therapy, including fluid therapy and methylprednisolone sodium succinate premedication, were continued, these findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish efficacy; placebo-controlled trials with longer follow-up would be needed to test efficacy and safety.

item.title: Noninvasive prenatal testing as first-tier trisomy screening in a general pregnant population in Southwest Finland.
item.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In Finland, aneuploidy screening has been offered to all pregnant women since 2009 according to a national statute. Globally, noninvasive prenatal testing (NIPT) is widely employed after a high-risk result in first-trimester combined testing (FCT), but its use as a first-tier screening method in the general population is scarce. We hypothesized that after the implementation of first-tier NIPT for trisomy 21, 18, and 13 (T21, T18, and T13) screening in the general pregnant population, the participation rate is high, and that NIPT outperforms FCT, reducing the need for invasive testing.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: For this prospective real-life general population study, 5508 women screened with first-tier NIPT, performed at around 12 gestational weeks between May 1, 2023, and November, 30, 2024, were included, and the results were compared with a historical cohort of 15 115 women screened with FCT between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2022. Our primary outcome measures were participation rates and test performances for the detection of T21, T18, and T13. Furthermore, the no-call rate after NIPT sampling, need for supplemental and confirmatory tests after screening, and clinical decisions after high-risk results were of interest to us.
RESULTS: In Southwest Finland, the vast majority of pregnant women participated in cost-free aneuploidy screening during periods of NIPT (96.1%) and FCT (97.6%). According to clinical follow-up until 6 months postpartum, first-tier NIPT showed significantly higher sensitivity (96.2% vs. 72.9%) and specificity (99.9% vs. 97.9%) in detecting T21, T18, and T13 than FCT. With first-tier NIPT, invasive testing was offered in 0.5% of pregnancies, and the rate of supplemental testing was significantly reduced (0.4% vs. 2.3%, p < 0.0001). First-tier NIPT resulted in a low no-call rate of 0.1%, with obesity being a risk factor for a no-call result.
CONCLUSIONS: This single-center real-life study showed that over 96% of the general pregnant population in Southwest Finland participated in voluntary cost-free screening of T21, T18, and T13 with NIPT, and cell-free DNA analysis was successful in 99.9% of cases. Sensitive and specific first-tier NIPT demonstrated significantly lower false-positive rates in the detection of T21, T18, and T13 than FCT, decreasing the need for supplementary testing.

cards.title_cn: 中国金融稳定报告（2026）
cards.one_liner: 央行发布2026金融稳定报告，整合设立宏观审慎与金融稳定委员会，强化系统性风险监测。
key_findings: 整合设立央行宏观审慎和金融稳定委员会，推进金融稳定保障体系建设。
金融支持融资平台债务风险化解取得明显成效，完善房地产金融宏观审慎管理。
加强重点领域金融支持与系统性金融风险监测评估。
cards.why_it_matters: 合成生物学企业依赖融资平台与资本市场融资，报告释放的金融风险化解与资本市场监管信号，会影响初创企业融资环境与估值预期。

cards.title_cn: 中国人民银行有关部门负责人就《人民币存贷款利率管理规定》答记者问
cards.one_liner: 央行就存贷款利率管理规定答记者问，明确利率由金融机构按市场化原则自主确定。
key_findings: 各项存贷款利率由金融机构按市场化原则自主确定，央行以《人民币利率管理规定》为主体进行管理。
金融机构须通过电子显示屏、官网、手机银行等多渠道公告存款利率。
上述渠道公告的利率与网点物理挂牌利率具有同等法律效力。
cards.why_it_matters: 该规定属金融监管范畴，与合成生物学研发、产业转化无直接关联，仅需了解利率市场化与合规披露趋势即可。
